### workspace relaunch --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace relaunch [--name WS | --all] [--json] [workspace1] [workspace2] ...

Stop active workspaces and relaunch them.
With no workspace named, relaunches the workspace the current directory is in.
Before this changed, bare `relaunch` relaunched every active workspace; pass --all for that.
Outside any workspace, name one or pass --all.
A workspace that isn't active is refused before anything stops (workspace_not_active).

        --name NAME                  Workspace to relaunch; positional names may be given too
        --all                        Relaunch every active workspace (what bare relaunch used to do)
        --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md) instead of progress text;
                                     the text goes to stderr. Exit 0, 3 when some projects failed, 1 when all did

Examples:
  workspace relaunch    # stop the workspace you are in and relaunch it
  workspace relaunch --all    # stop every active project and relaunch it (headless ones stay headless)
  workspace relaunch my-notes billing    # relaunch two projects
  workspace relaunch --all --json    # a script relaunching everything and checking the result
  workspace relaunch --all --json 2>/dev/null    # keep the progress text out of the way when piping the document
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace relaunch
